questions.prompt: Whose assassination in Sarajevo helped trigger the First World War?
questions.explanation: The assassination of Austro-Hungarian heir Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914 set off the July Crisis that escalated into war.

sources.displayName: Imperial War Museums - How the world went to war in 1914

questions.prompt: What was the Allied code name for the 1944 campaign to invade Normandy?
questions.explanation: Operation Overlord was the Allied campaign to establish a lodgment in Normandy; its assault phase began on D-Day, 6 June 1944.

questions.prompt: Which international organization was created under the Treaty of Versailles settlement?
questions.explanation: The Covenant of the League of Nations formed part of the Versailles settlement after the First World War.

sources.displayName: U.S. Office of the Historian - The Paris Peace Conference and the Treaty of Versailles

questions.prompt: The Battle of Midway was a pivotal naval battle in which theatre of the Second World War?
questions.explanation: U.S. and Japanese carrier forces fought near Midway Atoll in June 1942, changing the strategic balance in the Pacific.

sources.displayName: U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command - Battle of Midway

questions.prompt: What was Bletchley Park's principal wartime role?
questions.explanation: Bletchley Park was the center of British wartime codebreaking, where intercepted Axis communications were analyzed and decrypted.

sources.displayName: Bletchley Park - The story of Bletchley Park

questions.prompt: What was the central objective of the wartime Manhattan Project?

options.text: Design the first Allied jet aircraft

questions.explanation: The U.S.-led Manhattan Project coordinated the scientific and industrial effort that produced the first atomic weapons during the Second World War.

sources.displayName: U.S. Department of Energy - Manhattan Project National Historical Park

questions.prompt: The United States became a member of the League of Nations after the First World War.
questions.explanation: The U.S. Senate rejected the Treaty of Versailles, so the United States never joined the League of Nations.

sources.displayName: United States Senate - The Senate Rejects the Treaty of Versailles
